chunks: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'This river of yours — meaning the water of the Euphrates — two water-spouts from the spouts of Paradise pour into it.'
He (the narrator) said: So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Had there been miles between us and it, we would have gone to it and sought water from it.'

key_terms.الجنة: Paradise; the celestial garden promised to the righteous
key_terms.الفرات: The Euphrates River; in Islamic tradition, one of the four rivers of Paradise
key_terms.ميزابان: Dual form of mizab (water-spout/gutter); two channels linking Paradise to the Euphrates
key_terms.نستسقي: To seek or draw water; a verb implying purposeful journey for the blessing of sacred water

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the Euphrates river and Paradise?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) affirms the sacred status of the Euphrates River by declaring that two water-spouts from Paradise pour into it, elevating it above ordinary rivers. When this tradition was narrated in Imam al-Sadiq's (AS) presence, the Imam expressed the profound spiritual esteem in which the Ahl al-Bayt held the Euphrates, stating they would travel even great distances to drink from it. This hadith belongs to a tradition within Shia literature that recognizes certain terrestrial elements as spiritually connected to the divine realm.
word_analysis: we would have gone to it
